name: Jasmin Paris
one_line: Won a 268-mile race outright against all the men, then became the first woman ever to finish the Barkley Marathons - with 99 seconds to spare.

facts.claim: won the 2019 Montane Spine Race OUTRIGHT - 268 miles along the Pennine Way in winter - beating every man in the field
facts.note: Wikipedia: 'the first woman to win the event overall.' Non-stop winter race.

facts.claim: her Spine time, 83 hours 12 minutes, smashed the overall course record - previously 95 hours 17 minutes - by twelve hours
facts.note: She didn't edge the record held by men - she took HALF A DAY off it.

facts.claim: second place in the 2019 Spine Race, Eoin Keith, finished 15 hours behind her
facts.note: Her nearest male rival at the time, Eugeni Rosello Sole, pressed his emergency button 6km from the finish with hypothermia - the field wasn't just beaten, it was broken.

facts.claim: during breaks in the Spine Race she expressed milk for her baby daughter
facts.note: Wikipedia verbatim: 'During breaks in the race she expressed milk for her baby.' Report flatly - the fact needs no decoration.

facts.claim: in 2024 became the first woman ever to finish the Barkley Marathons, in 59:58:21 - 99 seconds inside the 60-hour cutoff
facts.note: Confirmed by CNN/ESPN/iRunFar. Collapsed at the yellow gate at 5:16pm, 22 March 2024, Frozen Head State Park, Tennessee.

facts.claim: the Barkley: 100 miles in five loops, roughly 60,000 feet of climb, unmarked course, hidden books as checkpoints, 60-hour limit
facts.note: 60,000 ft is roughly twice Everest from sea level. Runners tear a page from each hidden book to prove passage.

facts.claim: in the race's history through 2024, only 20 people had ever finished it; she is the only woman
facts.note: iRunFar: 2024's five finishers 'brought the total number of people to complete the course to 20.' Hundreds attempt; say 'twenty people ever' not an attempts ratio (attempt counts vary by source).

facts.claim: she is a senior lecturer in veterinary studies at the University of Edinburgh; her PhD was in leukemia research; two children
facts.note: Running is effectively her side job. Born Manchester, 1983.

comparison.second_label: the old course record - 95:17, set by a man
comparison.gap_description: 83:12 against the old record of 95:17 - twelve hours removed.

story_beat: At the 2024 Barkley Marathons she reached the final stretch with the 60-hour cutoff nearly gone, sprinted uphill after 100 miles and 60,000 feet of climb, and collapsed against the yellow gate having beaten the clock by 99 seconds - the first woman to finish in the race's history.
